title: Pauri 26, meaning: priceless
hook: priceless His virtues and His dealings; many have described Him and gone on describing (Japji 26)

segments.voice: Yesterday, vaapaar, the trade, and your line, amul gun: priceless the virtues, priceless the trade. Today, the word amul itself.

Ask what someone would carry out of a burning house, and it's rarely the TV. It's a grandfather's photo, a child's first shoes, a cheap ring that belonged to someone. Put any of those up for sale online and they're worth almost nothing. Try to take them away and they're worth everything. The price tag and the value have nothing to do with each other. Pauri 26 takes that feeling, applies it to everything, and then asks who could ever describe it.
screen: `OUT OF A BURNING HOUSE.` → `WORTHLESS TO SELL.` → `PRICELESS TO YOU.`

segments.voice: Amul: a, not; mul, price. Priceless. Not expensive, which still has a number. Beyond numbers altogether. Pauri 26 stamps it on everything. In paraphrase: priceless the virtues and the trade, the traders and the storehouses. Priceless those who come, priceless what they carry away. Priceless the love, and priceless those absorbed in it. Priceless the law and the court, the scales and the weights, the blessings and the signs of grace, the command itself. Then, in the original: amulo amul aakhiaa na jaae. Priceless beyond priceless, it can't be told. Then a long, wide turn. Many describe it, the stanza says, in paraphrase. The Vedas and the Puranas; the learned, with their commentaries. Brahmas and Indras. The gopis and Govind. Shiva, and the siddhas. Gods and demons, humans, sages and servants. So many have described it and gone on describing, have spoken and risen and left. If as many again were made, they still couldn't tell it. Notice who's in that list: scriptures, gods and sages from the world Guru Nanak lived in. None of them is mocked. All are honored as describers, and all fall short, because the thing is amul. It's as great as it wishes to be, and only the True One knows. So the lesson reaches all the way down to a pair of child's shoes. The most valuable things don't have a price. They're not less real for that. They're more.
screen: `AMUL — BEYOND ANY NUMBER.` · `AMULO AMUL AAKHIAA NA JAAE.` · `VEDAS, GODS, SAGES DESCRIBE.` · `ALL FALL SHORT; NONE MOCKED.` · then, large: `PRICELESS, ALL OF IT.`

segments.voice: Choose one ordinary thing near you: a cup, your own hand, the chair, the light through the window. Look at it as if it were priceless and couldn't be replaced: its shape, its color, what it does for you, who made it, how long it has served. Let it be amul for a while, then close your eyes and rest.
Amul. Priceless: a, not, and mul, price. Pauri 26 says it of every virtue and every dealing, and says no describer, however great, can tell it all.
Your line: priceless, all of it. Even the Vedas fell short of telling it. See you tomorrow.

howItsDone: Pauri 26 is recited in the morning Japji Sahib; many Sikhs hear its long list of describers, from the Vedas to the gods and sages, as a reminder that no one can fully tell the worth of the One.

fork.setup: the Vedas, the gods, the sages have all tried to describe the One. what does Pauri 26 say if as many again were made?
options: they would argue with each other.
fork.reveal: so many have described it and gone on describing; if as many again were made, they still couldn't tell it. it's amul.

original.note: Gurmukhi: amul, priceless; a (not) + mul (price). Japji Pauri 26 repeats it line after line.

trapdoor: what you thought: priceless means very, very expensive.
what it means: beyond any price at all, too valuable to measure, and too great for any describer to tell.
what a scholar hears: amul, a- plus mul, parallels asankh; the stanza names the Vedas, Puranas, Brahmas, Indras, gopis and Govind, Shiva and the siddhas as describers who all fall short.

sources.ref: Guru Granth Sahib, Ang 5–6 (Japji, Pauri 26, the priceless lines and the describers)

notes: List of describers paraphrased; the line 'aakhahi kete keete budh' is left out because readings differ (many Buddhas / many wise ones). Confirm.
The closing lines about the one who claims to describe being the fool of fools are left out; confirm.
Gurmukhi ਅਮੁਲੁ; the stanza also has ਅਮੁਲ and ਅਮੁਲੋ. Confirm preferred form.
